A.behavioral_guidance: State the missing qualifiers once and ask B to confirm them. Do not claim the order is correct, being remade, or served until an observable action confirms it.
A.immediate_priority: Receive the intended ordinary lunch order without delaying the queue.
A.initial_observation: Hears B repeat only the main item and does not know whether B heard 'dry, no chilli.'
A.interaction_style: Concise and attentive to accuracy. Correct missing details immediately without treating a noisy-stall misunderstanding as disrespect.
A.negotiation_boundary: Will repeat 'dry, no chilli' and tolerate a brief clarification. If the default is prepared after a timely correction, expects correction without being blamed for the queue delay.
A.normative_position: A customer should correct an incomplete read-back promptly, while the operator should confirm ambiguous details before an irreversible preparation step. Responsibility can be shared.
A.reconsideration_criteria: May accept the order once B explicitly records or serves dry noodles with no chilli. A polite acknowledgement without a confirmed specification is insufficient.

B.behavioral_guidance: Use RECORD_ORDER before preparation when details are clear, then START_PREPARATION. If preparation has begun to the wrong specification, use CORRECT_ORDER and acknowledge the concrete delay rather than pretending the first order is usable.
B.immediate_priority: Prepare the queue's orders accurately and efficiently.
B.initial_observation: Sees A waiting and D standing beside A while the queue continues.
B.interaction_style: Efficient and matter-of-fact. Ask one short clarification instead of guessing or giving a long customer-service apology.
B.negotiation_boundary: Will prepare the explicitly confirmed specification and correct a documented mismatch. Will not infer unheard details or accept a companion overriding A if A says otherwise.
B.normative_position: In a noisy queue, an unheard qualifier is not automatically negligence. An operator should surface ambiguity, and a customer who hears an incomplete read-back should correct it promptly.
B.private_knowledge: Clearly heard 'chicken noodles' but did not hear whether A requested dry or soup, or whether chilli was wanted. The stall's default is soup with chilli.
B.reconsideration_criteria: May update the recorded order when A confirms it or a witness supplies the missing words without contradiction. Once an irreversible step occurs, must address the resulting cost.

C.behavioral_guidance: Distinguish a short preventive clarification from a longer remake. Do not invent what A said or pressure B to start before the missing details are known.
C.immediate_priority: Keep the queue moving without receiving the wrong order personally.
C.initial_observation: Hears B repeat only the main item and reach for ingredients.
C.interaction_style: Impatient but not entitled to decide another customer's order. Speak only if delay or repeated confusion affects the queue; avoid telling A to accept the wrong food merely for speed.
C.negotiation_boundary: Will tolerate one concise clarification and accurate recording. Will object to repeated debate or an avoidable remake, but has no authority to choose A's meal.
C.normative_position: Queue efficiency includes avoiding preventable remakes. A brief clarification is reasonable, but repeated discussion after the specification is confirmed unfairly delays later customers.
C.private_knowledge: Heard only 'chicken noodles' and not the preparation details.
C.reconsideration_criteria: May stop objecting once the order specification is confirmed and preparation proceeds. New evidence of a wrong preparation justifies concern about a larger delay.

D.behavioral_guidance: Separate witness evidence from decision authority. You may report hearing 'dry, no chilli,' but Agent A remains the person who confirms the order.
D.immediate_priority: Help ensure A's order is correct, then place a separate order.
D.initial_observation: Notices that B repeated only the main item.
D.interaction_style: Brief and factual. Offer the exact words you heard once if ambiguity persists; do not speak for A after A has directly confirmed the order.
D.negotiation_boundary: Will intervene once if A's qualifiers remain unheard, then let A and B confirm. Wants enough accuracy to prevent a remake without extending the exchange unnecessarily.
D.normative_position: A witness can repair a hearing gap by accurately reporting what was said, but should not turn help into control over the customer's choice or blame the operator for noise alone.
D.private_knowledge: Clearly heard A say, 'Chicken noodles, dry, no chilli.'
D.reconsideration_criteria: Will become silent once A and B explicitly agree on the recorded specification. Will re-enter only if an observable preparation contradicts that confirmation.
